$comment: Illustration slot tracker (DESIGN-002 §Illustration slots). Each slot is {status, file, alt}: status 'real' = house-style SVG in src/assets/svg (SlotArt renders it as an with the alt text below), 'lab-owned' = the renderer draws its own scene inline. Hotspot bases (scene-atv-anatomy, scene-trail-hazards) are authored on a 500x300 (5:3) canvas and composed so the curriculum's hotspot x/y percentages land on the named features — present them at their intrinsic 5:3 ratio (SlotArt ratio="5 / 3") so percent coordinates stay exact.

hero-landing.alt: A helmeted rider seated on a utility ATV on a blazed trail, drawn as a flat field-guide plate with contour lines and waypoint blazes.

hero-m1-mindset.alt: A rider stands at a trail junction, scan line tracing the blazed left route while an unmarked route fades right — choosing the line before riding it.

hero-m2-machine.alt: Side view of a utility ATV drawn as a field-guide plate, with callout ticks at the handlebars, rear rack, front tire, and footwells.

hero-m3-gear.alt: Flat-lay plate of the riding kit: full-face helmet, padded gloves, and over-ankle boots arranged like museum specimens.

hero-m4-terrain.alt: A hillside drawn as nested contour rings with a switchback trail climbing to the summit and caution cues marking the steep face.

hero-m5-environment.alt: A storm front crossing a valley trail, drawn map-style with a cold-front line, rain over the west ridge, a compass rose, and a scale bar.

hero-m6-roads.alt: Bird's-eye view of a trail meeting a paved road at a marked crossing: the rider stopped square at the stop bar with sight lines drawn both ways.

scene-atv-anatomy.alt: Side view of a single-rider utility ATV with its systems in place: low-pressure tires, front brake caliper, coil-over suspension, engine, frame tube, footwell running boards, handlebars, and front and rear cargo racks.

scene-walkaround-top.note: The walkaround lab renderer authors its own interactive top-view scene inline; SlotArt keeps the designed placeholder for this slot.

scene-helmet-fit.alt: Cross-section of a helmet on a rider's head showing shell, impact liner, and comfort padding as layers, with the strap V fastened and a two-finger brow-gap check drawn at the rim.

scene-trail-hazards.alt: A mid-morning forest trail dipping through a drainage, broadcasting seven cues: a blind crest, an off-camber section, shadowed ruts, a dark wet patch at the low point, gravel over hardpack on the climb out, a downed limb screened by brush, and a soft undercut edge above the water.

scene-crossing.alt: Bird's-eye view of an ATV stopped square behind the stop bar at a road crossing, sight lines swept in both directions along the road and a vehicle approaching from the left.

scene-loading-cargo.alt: Rear-view comparison of rack loading: a low, centered, strapped case with a low center of gravity beside a tall loose stack whose high center of gravity tips the machine.

badge-b-mindset.alt: Clear Eyes badge: an eye with a trail blaze for a pupil.

badge-b-mechanic.alt: Walkaround Ready badge: a wrench crossed over a tire.

badge-b-geared.alt: Geared Up badge: a full-face helmet.

badge-b-terrain.alt: Terrain Reader badge: an eye scanning contour lines.

badge-b-prepared.alt: Storm Smart badge: a storm cloud read with a compass.

badge-b-roadwise.alt: Road Wise badge: a marked road-crossing sign.

badge-b-journal.alt: Field Scribe badge: a field notebook and pen.

badge-b-scholar.alt: Sharp Eye badge: a checkmark striking a target.

badge-b-graduate.alt: Sightline Graduate badge: a summit flag over the range, flanked by laurels.

empty-journal.alt: An open, blank field notebook with ruled pages, a bookmark ribbon, and a pen lying ready.

empty-tutor.alt: Ranger's campaign hat beside a compass with its needle set — ready for a question.

state-404.alt: A dotted route running off the torn edge of a trail map; the signpost's second board hangs askew, pointing nowhere.

state-locked.alt: A padlocked gate across the trail; beyond it the route continues, faded, toward the next blaze.

cert-seal.alt: Circular certificate seal: rope border, pine ring, and a clay trail blaze bearing a summit line at the center.

act-content.note: Stacked text lines with a short last line - a screen of reading.

act-prediction-reveal.note: A cover lifted clear of the card beneath it, revealing what was hidden.

act-multiple-choice.note: Three option rows, the first marked with a tick.

act-sort-categorize.note: Items dropping down a splitting chute into two bins.

act-match.note: Two columns of items with one pair joined by a connecting line.

act-hotspot-list.note: A picture frame with a pulsing point of interest at its centre.

act-branching-decision.note: A trail that forks, then forks again - three outcomes.

act-structured-response.note: A ruled writing box with a pen resting on the first line.

act-journal-builder.note: A field notebook with a plus - adding a page to the journal.

act-reflection.note: A thought arc rising over the trail line - looking back at the ride.

act-lab-objective.note: A slider control set over a wedge - a lab you adjust and observe.

act-checkpoint.note: A pennant flag on a post - the checkpoint at the end of a lesson.

topic-mindset.note: An eye above a forking trail - judgment applied at a decision point.

topic-machine.note: A spoked wheel with its hub - the machine and its upkeep.

topic-gear.note: A full-face helmet seen head on - the riding kit.

topic-terrain.note: Three nested contour arcs rising to a summit - reading the ground.

topic-environment.note: A cloud crossing a ridge line - weather over the terrain.

topic-roads.note: A crossroads seen from above - the trail meeting a road.

topic-general.note: An open field guide with a compass needle standing in the gutter - general knowledge beyond the course.

keylist-tcloc.alt: Five T-CLOC inspection zones drawn as stations around a machine and walked as an ordered loop, numbered one to five from the marked start station and returning to it.

keylist-six-decisions.alt: Six risk decisions - bare head, pavement, extra rider, impairment, wrong-size machine and outrunning your eyes - drawn as six equal marks at equal distance around one geared rider, each touching the rider: a set with no single villain.

keylist-three-leaks.alt: A judgment reservoir with its level fallen, draining through three separate outlets of equal size: group gravity pulling the last rider along, familiarity discounting a repeated trail, and sunk momentum pushing on into failing light.

keylist-fit-checks.alt: A seated rider measured against four independent pass-or-fail gates - reach, stance, leverage and machine class - each drawn as a dimension that either fits between the gate posts or does not.

keylist-helmet-consequences.alt: A helmet cross-section with the crushable liner highlighted as the mechanism, and four causal arrows out to the rules that follow from it: worn and fastened, fitted, rated, and crushable only once.
keylist-helmet-consequences.note: m3-l1-s1 already carries scene-helmet-fit (C-013, wave V1); VISUAL_ASSETS.md 7.3.0 permits one figure per step

keylist-stability-model.alt: One stability model at centre - centre of gravity held over the support base between the tires - with four applications around it: climbing slopes, side-hills, rider position as a control, and loads carried high.

keylist-four-families.alt: The four weather families split by what they degrade: water and light acting on the trail being read on the left, cold-and-heat and dust acting on the rider doing the reading on the right.

keylist-before-you-go.alt: The three before-you-go artifacts laid out before the ride: a ride plan with the route and turnaround marked, a communication plan naming who is told and when, and the carry kit strapped to the machine's rack.

keylist-stop-assess-communicate.alt: Stop, assess and communicate drawn as a strict three-stage sequence numbered one to three, each stage passing through a gate that only the previous stage opens.

keylist-pavement-physics.alt: Three engineering facts - a tire built to deform, a locked rear axle, and a high centre of gravity - with their arrows all converging on the same conclusion at the pavement.

keylist-good-crossing.alt: A road crossing broken into four numbered steps: stop completely at the bar, look both ways along the road, cross square to the road and briskly, and cross one machine at a time.
keylist-good-crossing.note: m6-l2-s1 already carries scene-crossing (C-011, wave V1); one figure per step

keylist-three-standards.alt: Three standards posted as signs at one trail junction - zero impairment, yielding generously to others, and staying on designated trail - applying to whichever branch is taken.

match-thumb-throttle.alt: Thumb throttle: the hand stays closed around the grip while the thumb alone works a small lever on the bar.

match-front-brake.alt: Front brake: a hand lever hinged at a perch beside the grip and swept out in front of the handlebar.

match-rear-brake.alt: Rear brake: an over-the-ankle boot with its toe down on the foot pedal pad, the pedal arm swept back to its pivot.

match-stop-switch.alt: Engine stop switch: a proud rocker in a raised bezel, thrown to the side marked by a bold stop bar so it can be found by feel.

match-gear-selector.alt: Gear selector: a routed gate plate with the lever seated at the bottom of the deep leg, chevrons marking the low range.

match-body-position.alt: Body position, the invisible control: a helmeted rider standing on the footboards with weight moved forward over the bars, the direction of the lean marked in clay.

match-turnaround-time.alt: Turnaround time: a clock face above a U-turn arrow — the hour you head back, fixed before you leave.

match-off-ride-contact.alt: Off-ride contact: someone at home at a lit window with a phone, waiting on the check-in — a person who is not on the ride.

match-water-food.alt: Water and food beyond the plan: a part-full bottle beside a ration bar pushed up out of its wrapper.

match-nav.alt: Signal-free navigation: a folded paper map with a compass laid across its corner — neither needs a phone or a signal.

match-warmth.alt: Warmth for an unplanned wait: a quilted insulating layer folded down into a stack, collar showing.

section-briefing.alt: Briefing section: a trailhead post with its board pointing the way out.

section-learn.alt: Learn section: the field guide open on its spine.

section-try.alt: Try section: a boot sole pressed into the trail.

section-debrief.alt: Debrief section: a backward glance, the arc turning to look down the trail already ridden.

section-journal.alt: Journal section: a pen set to the ruled line.

section-checkpoint.alt: Checkpoint section: the trail blaze on its post, the mark you ride to.

sort-gear-helmet.alt: A rated full-face helmet with the chin strap fastened through its buckle.

sort-gear-eyes.alt: Riding goggles on a head strap — eye protection for every ride.

sort-gear-boots.alt: A riding boot whose shaft stands well above the ankle line.

sort-gear-gloves.alt: A riding glove with a fastened cuff — hands covered on every ride.

sort-gear-longs.alt: A long-sleeved jersey and full-length trousers — arms and legs covered.

sort-gear-chest.alt: A chest and roost protector — body armour added when conditions call for it.

sort-gear-hiviz.alt: A high-visibility whip flag on its mast — being seen when conditions hide you.

sort-gear-layers.alt: Weather layers stacked with the outer shell on top of the insulation.

sort-gear-loose.alt: A loose scarf trailing into a turning wheel — never worn on the machine.

sort-gear-flipflops.alt: A flip-flop sandal — footwear that never goes on the machine.

sort-gear-headphones.alt: Headphones sealing both ears — hearing shut off, never on the machine.

sort-cond-dust.alt: A machine riding into a dust cone with the trail ahead lost from view.

sort-cond-wet-roots.alt: A band of wet roots crossing the trail — slow down and add space.

sort-cond-frost.alt: Frost still lying in shade after sun-up — slow down and add space.

sort-cond-fading-light.alt: A clock against a sun already setting on the horizon — change the route or the schedule.

sort-cond-storm.alt: A weather front line with rain falling behind it — change the route or the schedule.

sort-cond-swollen-creek.alt: A creek running high and fast between its banks, well over its normal level — change the route.

sort-cond-cold-hands.alt: A hand gone cold and stiff on the brake lever — stop and tend the rider.

sort-cond-heat.alt: Hard sun and a water bottle already empty — stop and tend the rider.

sort-cargo-kid-behind.alt: A second person carried behind the operator on a single-seat machine — never done.

sort-cargo-two-up.alt: A purpose-built two-seat machine carrying two geared riders in their own seats.

sort-cargo-rack-limits.alt: A low load strapped down on the rack, inside its posted weight limit.

sort-cargo-heavy-high.alt: A tall load riding high on the rack, lifting the machine's centre of gravity — check it first.

sort-cargo-towing.alt: A machine towing a small trailer — check the hitch and the load before you go.

sort-cargo-lap.alt: A small child riding on the operator's lap, over the controls — never done.

sort-cargo-loose-tools.alt: Unsecured tools bouncing loose in the front basket — secure them before you go.

inset-tires.alt: Close-up of a low-pressure ATV tire under load: the rim stays perfectly round while the carcass squats, bulges at the sidewall and moulds itself over a stone, spreading into a long contact patch instead of the single point a rigid wheel would make.

inset-handlebars.alt: The handlebar cluster as the rider looks down on it: engine stop switch under the left thumb, brake lever standing off the right grip, and the thumb throttle hinged at the inboard end of that grip — the only control feeding the engine.

inset-brakes.alt: Behind the front wheel: a vented brake disc turning inside the rim with the caliper clamped over its edge, and a hose running up to the master cylinder and lever at the handlebar, so the whole squeeze-to-clamp circuit is visible at once.

inset-suspension.alt: A coil-over shock caught part way through its travel: the frame holds its line, the lower arm swings down, the spring compresses, and the tire stays pressed into a rock — with the stroke still held in reserve marked alongside the shock.

inset-engine.alt: The engine mass with the fuel tank sitting on it, marked with the two walkaround stops joined by one check line: the fuel filler cap on top and the oil sight glass on the crankcase.

inset-footwells.alt: An over-the-ankle boot planted flat on the footpeg inside the running board, with the heel guard drawn as the wall standing between that foot and the rear wheel turning just behind it.

inset-racks.alt: A rear cargo rack carrying a low, centred case strapped down through both rails, with the posted rack limit tag hanging off the side and the load's centre of gravity marked sitting low and over the middle of the rack.

inset-chassis.alt: The same machine with its bodywork dropped back to a hairline so only the frame tubes remain, and the load path traced through them: rack rail into the backbone, along the backbone, out through the suspension mounts and down into the contact patches.

inset-crest.alt: A blind crest read as a cue: the trail's edges converge as it climbs and the surface simply stops at the ridge line. The far side of the valley is visible in the distance, everything between is not, and the sight distance is marked ending at the crest.

inset-side-slope.alt: Cross-section of an off-camber trail bench cut into a hillside: the far edge sits below the near edge, the surface line is measured against level to show the drop, and every sapling on the slope leans the same way, downhill.

inset-shadow-rut.alt: A tree shadow lying across the trail: straight over flat ground, and kinking down and back out where it crosses each rut. The bend in a line that should have been straight is the only thing that gives a rut away in flat light.

inset-wet-clay.alt: The low point of a drainage dip: the trail surface changes colour and goes darker and smoother well before any standing water appears, with runoff arriving from both slopes and a shallow pool collecting at the bottom. The dry-to-damp edge is marked.

inset-loose-over-hard.alt: Cut through the tread: a thin sheet of loose gravel lying on a hard packed base nothing keys into, a wheel track that has already ploughed the loose layer aside, and the stones thrown clear and piled on the verges. The interface between loose and hard is marked.

inset-deadfall.alt: A downed limb read as a cue: one horizontal line lying across a stand of vertical trunks, broken into fragments by brush screening it, with the line the eye has to complete across those gaps drawn in.

inset-soft-edge.alt: Section through an undercut trail edge: the tread runs on well past the ground beneath it, cracks run parallel to the lip, chunks have already broken away, roots hang in the shadow of the void, and the water that took the toe out is still working at it.
